mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 4% over the prior 4 months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by at least 0.5 percentage points over the last 4 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the 4-month FEDFUNDS change (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL inflation rate crosses above 2% for two consecutive months, market expectations for future rate cuts diminish, causing a short-term decline in S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 2.0% and remains above for at least two months
failure_condition: A 20-day T-bill yield premium over 5-year SPX futures turns negative (implying lower expected returns) during the inflation crossing period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly PAYEMS (labor market activity) coincides with stronger corporate hiring signals, which pre-emptively boosts investor confidence and drives positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 10% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns show no correlation with PAYEMS changes after controlling for GDP growth and unemployment (R-squared < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both GDPC1 (goods demand) and HOUST (housing starts) over the prior quarter suggests a dual softening in consumption and investment, which predicts negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < GDPC1 previous quarter AND HOUST < HOUST previous quarter
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically different from a baseline of neutral (0%) when both proxies are in decline (two-tailed t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly expansion in INDPRO (industrial production) exceeding 2% while UNRATE remains below 7% indicates supply-side strength without labor cost pressures, which typically supports positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by >2% month-over-month AND UNRATE < 7%
regime_hint: robust supply expansion with low wage inflation
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant relationship with the combined INDPRO/UNRATE pattern (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 5% for three consecutive months, lower borrowing costs for consumers and businesses increase spending and investment, producing positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or flat despite the three-month UNRATE decline (out-of-sample test).

mechanism_narrative: During a sustained period where FEDFUNDS remains below 1% and RSAFS (reserves) grows, liquidity conditions in financial markets relax, which tends to drive positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant effect after controlling for S&P 500 volatility (F-statistic < 1.0).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a 'late-cycle expansion' characterized by rising consumer confidence (implied by positive HOUST) and low unemployment (implied by PAYEMS) predicts a sharp upward surprise in S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: regime: 'late-cycle expansion' AND HOUST increases AND PAYEMS increases
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not exhibit a statistically significant positive jump during confirmed late-cycle expansion periods (p > 0.05).
